description: A windowed polyphonic comparator giving the minimum, maximum, clamp and overflow of two voltages along with six comparison gates

params.text: Adds an offset of -10V to 10V to the A input
Adds an offset of -10V to 10V to the B input
Sets the tolerance, -10V to 10V, summed with the TOL input: how far A may be from B and yet count as equal; its absolute value is used, and MIN and MAX ignore it

inputs.text: One of the two compared voltages, summed with its OFFSET knob
The voltage A is compared against, summed with its OFFSET knob
Widens or narrows the equality window, added to the tolerance OFFSET knob

outputs.text: The instantaneous lower of the two compared voltages, unaffected by the tolerance
The instantaneous higher of the two compared voltages, unaffected by the tolerance
A clamped to within the tolerance either side of B
How far A lies outside that clamp, positive or negative, computed as A minus CLAMP
High while A is within the tolerance of B
High while A is further from B than the tolerance
High while A is at or below B plus the tolerance
High while A is at or above B minus the tolerance
High while A is below B minus the tolerance
High while A is above B plus the tolerance

menu: Gate voltages — the low and high voltages of the six comparison gates: 0,1 or +/-1 or 0,5 or +/-5 or 0,10, which is the default, or +/-10
Absolute value and Invert, in a signal output's own port menu — rectify that output, invert it, or both; a green light at the port marks absolute value and a red light marks inversion
B normalled to A -1 sample — feeds B the previous sample of A, so A>B, A<B and A=B report a rising, falling or flat slope on A
Oversample — Off, x2, x4, x8, x16 or x32, cutting aliasing on every output, the gates included, when working at audio rates
Oversample filter quality — 10th order by default, with 8th order and a cheaper 6th order; 10th and 8th cut at 80% of Nyquist and 6th at 50%
